title: Write-path gap for field-id-bound policy during schema evolution
summary: The messages here start with Sung Yun (sungwy) replying to Andrei about a broader pattern; Sung wanted the community to first decide whether the 'Drift' and 'Creation' problems described in a Google Doc, which have security consequences for fine-grained access control policies, merit a first-class construct in the REST catalog write path, and planned to bring the policy case to the catalog sync. Prashant Singh saw no gap: catalogs resolve column names to field IDs before persisting a policy attachment, and when ReadRestrictions was modeled, defining and attaching policies was intentionally left as a catalog concern. Sung agreed that binding by field ID addresses drift, but pointed out that a field ID does not exist until the schema change commits, leaving a window in which a new column meant to be protected is not; the question is whether to accept that or let a column land protected in the same commit. Yufei Gu (flyrain) considered this mostly a catalog implementation concern that the spec need not mandate. The thread ends before the sync discussion.

positions.stance: Because a field ID does not exist until the schema change commits, a new column is unprotected until a policy is attached out of band, and the community should decide whether to allow a column to be created already protected.
There is no gap, since policies are bound by field ID in catalog metadata and defining and attaching policies was intentionally left to the catalog.
This is mostly a catalog implementation concern; a catalog may support committing policy with DDL, but the REST spec need not mandate it.

outcome.note: The thread ends without agreement; the topic was put on the agenda of the REST catalog sync.
